channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Tajikistan and China to expand cooperation in science and technology
item.description: Tajikistan's Institute of Water Problems, Hydropower and Ecology hosted a meeting with representatives from China's Suzhou University of Science and Technology on September 23. Discussions focused on scientific and technological cooperation, joint initiatives within the 'One Belt - One Road' and SCO frameworks, and research in water resources, ecology, and climate change.

item.title: Uzbekistan to subsidize cotton sold on the exchange by 500,000 soums per ton
item.description: Uzbekistan will provide a subsidy of 500,000 soums per ton for cotton sold on the exchange, benefiting both farmers and clusters. Additionally, clusters growing cotton on their land will receive 1.5 million soums per hectare. Support measures for exporters and fruit/vegetable producers are also being introduced.

item.title: New 'Keskaner' Border Crossing to Appear Between Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan
item.description: A new border crossing, 'Keskaner,' will be established between Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan, doubling the size of the current 'Dostlik' crossing. This is expected to triple freight traffic and reduce border crossing times significantly. The project is linked to increased regional transport flows, including the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway.

item.title: China and Russia Account for Over Half of Kyrgyzstan's Foreign Trade
item.description: In January-July 2026, Kyrgyzstan's foreign trade turnover exceeded $10 billion. China and Russia remain the main economic partners, accounting for over 60% of total trade. Exports grew significantly in July, driven by precious metals and textiles, with Russia being the largest buyer of Kyrgyz products.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan recognized for best tax environment for innovators in Asia-Pacific
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's High Technology Park has received the Startup Ecosystem Awards 2026 for 'Best Tax Environment for Innovators in the Asia-Pacific Region.' This award highlights the country's supportive policies for technological advancement.

item.title: Tajikistan Discusses Labor Migration Approaches at Budapest Process Conference
item.description: A representative from Tajikistan's Ministry of Labor, Migration, and Employment participated in the 'Budapest Process' conference in Islamabad. The event focused on legal migration pathways, protecting migrant rights, and improving migration management. Tajikistan shared its experiences and cooperation with the International Centre for Migration Policy Development.

item.title: Former Afghan President Karzai Condemns Pakistani Airstrikes as 'Aggression'
item.description: Former Afghan President Hamid Karzai condemned recent Pakistani airstrikes on Kandahar, Khost, and Paktia provinces, calling them 'aggression.' He urged Islamabad to pursue good neighborly relations and warned of consequences. The Taliban also condemned the attacks, vowing retaliation.

item.title: Tajikistan and Seychelles Sign Visa-Free Travel Agreement
item.description: Tajikistan and Seychelles have signed an agreement allowing visa-free short-term stays for holders of diplomatic, service, official, and ordinary passports. The signing ceremony took place in New York on September 23, involving the foreign ministers of both countries.

item.title: Tajikistan's Defense Minister Demands Quality Autumn Conscription
item.description: Tajikistan's Defense Minister Emomali Sobirzoda has called for a high-quality autumn conscription drive. The directive was issued during a training meeting focused on preparing for the conscription of citizens into the armed forces. Favorable service conditions were also highlighted.

item.title: UN General Assembly Discusses Artificial Intelligence Risks and Regulation
item.description: Artificial intelligence was a key topic at the UN General Assembly's 81st session, with leaders warning of risks from autonomous weapons to job displacement. While some, like US President Trump, favored rapid development over global control, others urged for common rules and state oversight.

item.title: Andijan to Establish Special Fund for Women's Employment with $20 Million
item.description: Andijan will create a special fund to ensure women's employment, allocating $20 million for this purpose. This initiative aims to provide specific financial and organizational opportunities to support women's employment in the region.

item.title: Regional competition for women civil servants held in Dangara district
item.description: A regional tour of the Republican competition "Best Civil Servant Among Women" took place in Dangara district on September 22, 2026. Participants were assessed on political knowledge, legal education, professional skills, and communication etiquette. The event aims to promote continuous learning and women's active participation in public service, aligning with state policy on gender equality.

item.title: Andijan to invest 100 billion soums in fruit and vegetable processing
item.description: Andijan region plans to invest 100 billion soums in fruit and vegetable processing. A meeting chaired by the President outlined plans to increase the processing level to 30% by providing small-scale processing equipment to the population on lease.

item.title: Taliban Spokesman Condemns Pakistani Airstrikes on Afghanistan, Vows Retaliation
item.description: Taliban spokesman Zabihullah Mujahid stated that Pakistani airstrikes on Kandahar, Paktia, and Khost provinces killed four civilians. He condemned the attacks as aggression and vowed they would not go unanswered, suggesting Pakistan sought to mask domestic issues. Pakistan's information minister claimed the strikes were self-defense against alleged Taliban drone incursions.

item.title: US and Iran Hold Talks for First Time Since June on UN General Assembly Sidelines
item.description: US President Donald Trump believes a peace deal with Iran could be reached after the US midterm elections on November 3. He stated that Iran is waiting for the US election results. Representatives from the US and Iran met on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, marking their first contact since late June.

item.title: CAPIF 5 Forum on Internet Connectivity Kicks Off in Dushanbe
item.description: The fifth Central Asia Peering and Internet Connectivity Forum (CAPIF 5) began in Dushanbe on September 24, 2026. This is the first time the event is held in Tajikistan, gathering internet community representatives, providers, operators, and IT specialists from Central Asia and beyond. The forum, organized by RIPE NCC and Tajiktelecom, focuses on network connectivity and internet infrastructure development.

item.title: Germany Offers 800 Nursing Positions for Uzbek Healthcare Workers
item.description: Uzbekistan's mid-level healthcare professionals are invited to work in German clinics through the Globogate program, which offers 800 job openings. Participants will receive 10 months of free German language courses, with stipends, accommodation, and B2 certification costs covered. Visa and travel expenses are also included.

item.title: World Bank: Security Spending Dominates Taliban Administration's Budget
item.description: Security accounts for over 45% of the Taliban administration's spending this fiscal year, totaling $787 million, according to a World Bank report. This exceeds combined spending on education, health, agriculture, and infrastructure. The report also notes a slowdown in Afghanistan's economic momentum.

item.title: Tajikistan and FAO discuss food safety and agricultural development
item.description: Tajikistan's Food Security Committee met with the UN's Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) in Rome to discuss strengthening cooperation in food safety and agricultural production. Key topics included livestock, animal health, and the "One Health" principle. Discussions also covered plant protection and digitalization.

item.title: US Central Command Reports 115 Commercial Vessels Rerouted Due to Iran Naval Blockade
item.description: The U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) reported that 115 commercial vessels were forced to reroute in regional waters. This action is part of a naval blockade against Iran, implemented in response to Tehran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz. The blockade aims to enforce naval passage and has impacted global oil prices.

item.title: Andijan plans to create 70,000 high-paying jobs with $7 billion investment
item.description: Andijan plans to create 70,000 high-paying jobs by attracting $7 billion in investment to 1,000 hectares of land designated for industry and entrepreneurship.

item.title: Pakistan's Recent Bombings in Afghanistan: Investigating Objectives
item.description: An analysis explores the potential objectives behind Pakistan's recent bombing campaigns targeting areas within Afghanistan. The report examines the strategic and political motivations that may have driven these cross-border military actions.

item.title: Pakistan confirms airstrikes in Afghanistan targeting drone launch sites
item.description: Pakistan conducted airstrikes and drone strikes on 10 locations in Afghanistan early Thursday, targeting sites used for launching drones into Pakistani territory. Information Minister Attaullah Tarar stated the strikes were an act of self-defense following alleged incursions from Afghanistan. Local sources reported strikes in Khost, Kandahar, and Paktia provinces, with no reported casualties. Pakistan claims its air defense systems intercepted all drones launched from Afghanistan.

item.title: New technologies double cotton yield at Agrocluster Oltingul
item.description: Uzbekistan's Agrocluster Oltingul has doubled cotton yields using Xinjiang technology on 23 hectares of its 850-hectare fields. This method, involving double-row planting under film and drip irrigation, saves water by 40% and fertilizer by 30%. The initiative aligns with a December 2025 presidential decree aimed at boosting crop yields and resource efficiency in agriculture.

item.title: UNDP Constructs 205 Earthquake-Resistant Buildings in Nangarhar with South Korean Aid
item.description: The UNDP has built 205 earthquake-resistant buildings in Nangarhar, Afghanistan, with support from South Korea. The structures include homes and health centers, with 203 housing vulnerable families. The project also created jobs for 719 locals and restored irrigation for 500 acres of farmland.

item.title: Artificial intelligence center for youth established in Balykchy
item.description: An artificial intelligence center for youth has been established in Balykchy, Kyrgyzstan, following a presidential decree. The center, created by "Akademiya IT Star," aims to develop digitalization services export and provide IT training in marketing, programming, and robotics. It has created 100 jobs and offers IT services to over 500 businesses.

item.title: Intensive technologies boost fish farming efficiency in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: A fish farming project utilizing intensive technologies has been launched by "Chinobod real biznes" in Balykchy district, Kyrgyzstan. The project, costing 30 billion soms, produces 200 tons of fish meat and 2.5 million fry annually on a two-hectare area. It also includes a laboratory for water purification using chlorella.

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva attends UN session, holds meetings in New York
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva, Head of the Presidential Administration of Uzbekistan, attended the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York. She held bilateral meetings with the CEO of the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) to discuss joint projects in transport and healthcare, and with Google's Vice President regarding YouTube monetization.

item.title: Central Asian Experts Discuss Future of Regional Cooperation Amid Global Changes
item.description: An international expert meeting on Central Asia's independent strategies, regional security, and new cooperation formats was held in Cadenabbia, Italy. Organized by the Konrad Adenauer Foundation, the event gathered experts from the region to discuss what shapes Central Asian identity and the future of regional partnerships.

item.title: Balykchy Enterprise Produces Sports Equipment Meeting International Standards
item.description: The 'LB Sport' enterprise in Balykchy, Kyrgyzstan, manufactures sports equipment according to international standards, replacing imports. The project, costing 25 billion soums, produces 65 types of equipment for 18 sports, with an annual output of 500,000 units worth 75 billion soums. Exports reach $3 million annually to Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and CIS countries.

item.title: Uzbekistan actively prepares for the 5th Samarkand Human Rights Forum
item.description: Uzbekistan is actively preparing for the 5th Samarkand Human Rights Forum, scheduled for September 28-29 in Tashkent and Samarkand. The forum will focus on human rights, sustainable development, and international cooperation, marking anniversaries of key human rights pacts and declarations.

item.title: Shavkat Mirziyoyev Meets Residents and Entrepreneurs on Andijan Gastronomy Street
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev engaged with residents and entrepreneurs on Andijan's gastronomy street in the Orikzor neighborhood. The 1.2-kilometer street created 100 new jobs and can accommodate over 10,000 visitors daily.

item.title: Two Afghan Citizens Enter US Via Legal Exception to Refugee Policy
item.description: Afghan Evacuate (AfghanIOM) reports two Afghan citizens entered the US through a legal exception to current policies, utilizing the refugee admission program. AfghanIOM's director stated this admission served US national interests. Thousands of Afghans await resettlement.

item.title: President Mirziyoyev visits ecotourism complex in Asaka
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited an ecotourism complex in Asaka. Once fully operational, the facility is expected to provide 80 billion soums in services annually and contribute 3 billion soums to the local budget.

item.title: Uzbek Citizen Dies of Poisoning in Istanbul After Unofficial Treatment
item.description: An Uzbek citizen, Mohirano Meliyeva, died in Istanbul on September 19 due to poisoning from pharmaceutical agents. She was being treated at home by unofficial doctors, which worsened her condition. Despite being taken to hospital, doctors could not save her life. Her body was repatriated.

item.title: Shavkat Mirziyoyev Reviews Xinjiang Cotton Growing Method Using Drip Irrigation
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev reviewed the Xinjiang method of cotton cultivation, which uses drip irrigation and fertilization systems to deliver water and nutrients directly to the plant roots. This method reportedly saves up to 40% of water and nearly 30% of fertilizer.

item.title: Bishkek Residents Learn About Eco-Friendly Heating Systems
item.description: An informational meeting was held in Bishkek for residents interested in eco-friendly and energy-efficient heating systems, specifically heat pumps. Participants learned about preferential state loans for installation, equipment costs, and operational benefits, including during electricity supply restrictions. The project is supported by the World Bank.

item.title: Bishkek residents learn about eco-friendly heating systems
item.description: An informational meeting in Bishkek focused on state subsidized loans for eco-friendly heating systems. Attendees learned about loan conditions, borrower requirements, and eligible expenses. A supplier presented heat pump technology, its benefits, and installation. The project is supported by the World Bank.

item.title: US, Denmark, and Greenland sign defense agreement to expand US military presence
item.description: The US, Denmark, and Greenland have signed a security agreement allowing the US to expand its military presence on the island. The deal amends a 1951 defense treaty and could lead to two additional US military bases.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Kochkor District Still Addressing Aftermath of July Mudflows
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Minister of Emergency Situations visited Kochkor district in Naryn region to assess the consequences of July mudflows. Four out of five affected state railway sections are cleared, with plans for protective measures on the remaining one and a new mudflow channel.
